# Commit Check

This page describes how claudetto makes sure that a commit or a pull request of Claude has the attribution lines.
It is for a user who wants to know what `/claudetto:setup` writes, and how to turn the check off.
The harness only makes sure that Claude follows the guidelines of the settings.
The user can turn each part off.

## What It Does

Claude Code adds the attribution lines when it follows a reminder in the context.
The `attribution` slice sends the same reminder, and it adds three checks for the git commands that Claude runs.
A command that the user types in a terminal has no check.

| Part | When | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reminder | Before a prompt, and in the task of a subagent | Claude knows the commit line and the pull request line. |
| `commit-msg` hook | On each `git commit` of Claude | Git rejects a message that does not end with the commit line. |
| Bypass deny | Before a `git commit` that skips the hook | The call is denied with the reason. |
| Pull request check | After `gh pr create` or `gh pr edit`, and before a GitHub MCP write | Claude gets a note, or the call is denied, when the body lacks the pull request line. |

## The Commit Hook

`/claudetto:setup` writes the `env` keys `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>`, and `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>` to the settings.
They define a config-based hook of git: `hook.claudetto-attribution.event` is `commit-msg`, and `hook.claudetto-attribution.command` is the script.
Two more pairs set `hook.claudetto-attribution.enabled` and `hook.commit-msg.enabled` to `true`.
The `env` keys are in the command scope of git, which wins over the config of a repository.
So a repository that sets one of the `enabled` keys to `false`, or sets another `command` or `event`, does not remove the check.
A setup from an earlier version has two pairs, and a new run adds the two `enabled` pairs after them.
The setup adds the keys after the `GIT_CONFIG_*` keys of the user, keeps those keys, and changes nothing on a second run.
The hook runs next to the hooks of the repository, so it does not replace them.

The `attribution` hooks write the commit line of each model of the session to a file in `~/.claudetto/attribution/<session id>/`.
The script reads the files of the session in `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`.
The script accepts a message when the last line, after git removes the comments, is a recorded line.
It also accepts a message where a recorded line is a whole line of the trailers, such as before a `Signed-off-by` line.
A rejected commit prints a note with the lines, and Claude adds the line and commits again.
A commit with no session id, or with no recorded line, passes.
The `pre-push` hook of the AI policy checks only a push from a `Bash` call of Claude, which `CLAUDETTO_AGENT_CALL` marks.
The commit hook does not read that name.

## Turn It Off

Set `attribution.commit` to an empty string in the settings.
The next prompt empties the record files, so the hook passes.
Set `attribution.pr` to an empty string to turn off the pull request check.
Remove the four pairs of `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>` and `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>` of claudetto from `env`, and lower `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, to remove the hook itself.

## Git Version

The config-based hooks need git 2.54 or later.
An older git ignores the keys, so the check passes with no output.
`/claudetto:setup` runs `git --version` and says so when git is older than 2.54 or is missing.
The note names the `commit-msg` and `pre-push` checks, which do not run.
The reminder and the bypass deny work with each version of git.

## Bypass Deny

When the commit line is on, the slice denies these forms of a `git commit` of Claude:

- `--no-verify`, `-n`, and a cluster such as `-nm`.
- `-c core.hooksPath=...`, `-c hook.<name>...`, or `--config-env` of such a key on the commit.
- An assignment of `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_<n>`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_<n>`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM`, or `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM` in a command with a commit.
- An `export`, `declare`, `typeset`, `readonly`, `local`, or `unset` of one of those names in a command with a commit.
- `env -u <name>`, `env -i`, or `env --ignore-environment` before `git` in a command with a commit.
- `git commit-tree`, which writes a commit and runs no hook.

The Bash tool of Claude Code does not keep the env of one call for the next call, so a change of the env is a bypass only in the call that commits.

The check reads the command with the shell reader of the kernel, so a message that holds `-n` is not a bypass.

## Pull Request Check

After a `gh pr create` or `gh pr edit` call, the slice runs `gh pr view --json body`.
When the body does not end with the pull request line, Claude gets a note to fix it with `gh pr edit --body-file`.
The GitHub MCP tools `create_pull_request` and `update_pull_request` are denied before the call when the `body` lacks the line.
The check after the call fails open: a missing `gh`, no network, or an unreadable body adds no note.
